tips.title: Check under your sink monthly
tips.body: A slow drip under the sink can cause mold in days. Put a dry paper towel under pipes overnight -- if it is damp in the morning, call your Pro.

tips.title: Know where your main shutoff is
tips.body: If a pipe bursts you have seconds, not minutes. Walk your home now and find the main water shutoff valve. Mark it with a piece of tape.

tips.title: Hot water heater maintenance
tips.body: Flush your water heater tank once a year to remove sediment. Sediment buildup reduces efficiency and shortens the heater lifespan by years.

tips.title: Fix running toilets fast
tips.body: A running toilet wastes up to 200 gallons of water per day. The fix is usually a $5 flapper valve. Jiggling the handle is not a fix.

tips.title: Low water pressure diagnosis
tips.body: Low pressure in one fixture usually means a clogged aerator -- unscrew the tap nozzle and rinse it. Low pressure everywhere means call your Pro.

tips.title: Test your GFCI outlets quarterly
tips.body: The outlets with Test and Reset buttons in bathrooms and kitchens protect you from electric shock. Press Test -- the outlet should go dead. Press Reset to restore. If it does not work, replace it.

tips.title: Do not overload power strips
tips.body: Power strips are for laptops and lamps, not appliances. Microwaves, heaters, and fridges need their own dedicated wall outlet.

tips.title: Flickering lights mean a connection problem
tips.body: Occasional flickering is usually a bulb. Frequent flickering on multiple lights is a loose connection in your panel -- do not ignore it.

tips.title: Check your breaker panel yearly
tips.body: Look for breakers that feel warm, smell burnt, or have visible rust. Any of these is a professional call, not a DIY job.

tips.title: Outdoor outlets need weatherproof covers
tips.body: If your outdoor outlets do not have spring-loaded covers, replace the cover plate. Water and electricity are a dangerous combination.

tips.title: Change your air filter every 90 days
tips.body: A clogged filter makes your HVAC work harder, raises your energy bill, and reduces air quality. Mark your calendar right now.

tips.title: Clean your AC condenser coils annually
tips.body: The outdoor unit collects leaves and debris. Turn off power at the disconnect box, then gently rinse the fins with a garden hose from the inside out.

tips.title: Bleed your radiators in autumn
tips.body: Trapped air in radiators means uneven heat and higher bills. Use a radiator key to open the bleed valve until water drips out, then close it.

tips.title: Seal gaps around ductwork
tips.body: Leaky ducts can waste 20-30% of your heating and cooling. Use foil tape (not regular duct tape) to seal visible joints in accessible areas.

tips.title: Keep vents unblocked
tips.body: Furniture pushed against vents forces your system to overwork. Leave at least 12 inches of clearance around every supply and return vent.

tips.title: Fix squeaky floors with talcum powder
tips.body: Sprinkle talcum powder over a squeaky hardwood floor and work it into the cracks with a soft cloth. It lubricates the boards without any nails or tools.

tips.title: Doors sticking in summer
tips.body: Wood expands in humidity. A sticking door in summer usually self-corrects in winter. If it sticks year-round, the frame may have shifted -- call your Pro.

tips.title: Fill small wall holes properly
tips.body: Toothpaste and soap are temporary. Use spackle for holes under 1 inch. Feather the edges smooth and prime before painting or the patch will show.

tips.title: Re-caulk your bathroom yearly
tips.body: Cracked caulk around tubs and showers lets water into the wall. Strip the old caulk completely, dry the surface for 24 hours, then apply a fresh bead.

tips.title: Check deck boards for rot annually
tips.body: Poke deck boards with a screwdriver. Soft spots mean rot has started. A single rotted board caught early is a one-hour fix. Ignored for a season it can compromise the whole structure.

tips.title: Clean your dryer vent annually
tips.body: Lint in the dryer vent is a leading cause of house fires. Disconnect the vent hose and use a long brush to clear the full run to the outside.

tips.title: Descale your shower head monthly
tips.body: Fill a plastic bag with white vinegar, tie it over the shower head overnight. In the morning the mineral deposits dissolve and pressure returns.

tips.title: Clean refrigerator coils twice a year
tips.body: Dusty coils at the back or bottom of your fridge make the compressor work harder and shorten its life. Vacuum them with a brush attachment.

tips.title: Deep clean kitchen exhaust filters
tips.body: Mesh filters above your stove trap grease. Soak them in hot water with dish soap and baking soda for 30 minutes, then scrub and rinse.

tips.title: Sanitize your garbage disposal
tips.body: Cut a lemon in half and run both halves through the disposal followed by a cup of ice and a handful of coarse salt. Eliminates odor without chemicals.

tips.title: Always cut in before rolling
tips.body: Use a 2-inch angled brush to paint a 3-inch band along edges, corners, and trim before rolling. This prevents lap marks and gives clean lines.

tips.title: Do not skip primer on dark walls
tips.body: Painting a light color over a dark wall without primer will need 4 or more coats. One coat of primer cuts that to two. Always prime.

tips.title: Fix nail pops before repainting
tips.body: Nail pops push through paint over time. Drive a new screw 2 inches from the pop, countersink the nail, fill with spackle, sand flush, then paint.

tips.title: Store leftover paint correctly
tips.body: Press a piece of plastic wrap against the paint surface before replacing the lid to prevent a skin from forming. Store upside down in a temperature-stable room.

tips.title: Test your colour in natural light
tips.body: Paint a 12-inch square patch on the actual wall and observe it at different times of day before committing. Colour chips in a store look nothing like paint on a wall.

tips.title: Water deeply, not frequently
tips.body: Shallow daily watering trains roots to stay near the surface. Water deeply twice a week so roots grow deep and your lawn becomes drought-resistant.

tips.title: Mow high in summer
tips.body: Set your mower to cut at 3-4 inches in summer heat. Taller grass shades the soil, retains moisture, and crowds out weeds.

tips.title: Dethatch your lawn in autumn
tips.body: A layer of dead grass and roots over half an inch thick blocks water and nutrients. Rent a dethatcher or use a stiff rake before the first frost.

tips.title: Blow out irrigation lines before winter
tips.body: Water left in irrigation lines freezes and cracks the pipes. Connect an air compressor to blow out each zone before temperatures drop below freezing.

tips.title: Mulch garden beds in spring
tips.body: A 2-3 inch layer of mulch around plants suppresses weeds, retains moisture, and regulates soil temperature. Keep mulch 2 inches away from plant stems.

tips.title: Test smoke detectors monthly
tips.body: Press and hold the test button on every smoke detector. Replace batteries annually even if the detector still works. Replace the whole unit every 10 years.

tips.title: Rekey locks when you move in
tips.body: You never know how many copies of the previous owner's keys exist. Rekeying costs $20 per lock at a hardware store and is worth every cent.

tips.title: Check exterior door frames for rot
tips.body: A strong deadbolt means nothing if the door frame is rotted. Push firmly on your exterior door frames. Soft or spongy wood needs replacement before winter.

tips.title: Keep your garage code private
tips.body: Change your garage door code annually and never write it on the remote. A garage is often the easiest entry point into a home.

tips.title: Install door reinforcement plates
tips.body: Most forced entries happen at the door frame, not the lock. A $15 steel strike plate with 3-inch screws into the stud makes kick-in attacks dramatically harder.
